body:
This will print the warning every time the _draw function runs. Printing text to the log/console has a high performance impact so it shouldn't be done except where necessary. Also, this will flood user logs and take up a lot of space on disk over time. 

We really shouldn't be printing a warning to give users performance feedback

> There is already a warning log in this draw function, although it's not about performance but about the effects.

It's not the same, existing warning is used for invalid argument combination (`width < 0` and `aa`). Unlike it, not drawing `width > 0` multiline in a single draw call is not an user error.

> Any way, we should let users know the function is not working in the way they expected.

Why would you expect it to work differently? It is reasonable to mention it in the documentation, but not to spam warnings.
